cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic strip-woven Kente cloth with characteristic geometric weft-float patterns and warp stripes, a textile form strongly associated with the Ashanti (Akan) of Ghana.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, composed of 4 strips of rayon (or possibly silk), hand-woven and hand sewn together along the selvedges. The ground warp and weft are purely of yellow thread. A weft chequerboard pattern has been formed along the central area of the cloth using supplementary thread to create alternating blocks of two patterns which are separated by a line of white thread: the first uses threads of green, black and maroon to form a small check; the second uses discontinuous supplementary weft to form geometric patterns in red, green and blue thread. At both ends of the cloth is a variant pattern, using a second pair of heedles to weave two bands of solid blocks flanking a zig-zag pattern in red and black, that run across all four strips. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
